transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-27 10:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (NexaHealth - Head of ML), Jon Rivera (NexaHealth - Platform Eng), Sara Lim (NexaHealth - Security)

Summary (auto): quick check-in on onboarding progress, access setup for Dedicated pilot, initial benchmark results and follow ups on security docs. Some audio artefacts, occasional speaker mislabels.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off, today is our weekly POC sync, main focus is env readiness and access.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, hi, thanks, quick note, had a couple of interruptions this morning, so if I sound a bit scrambled, apologies.
[00:27] Liam: No worries. We got about 50 minutes, we wanted to walk through the bench results you shared and next steps for VPC and SSO.
[00:37] Jon: Yep, we posted the initial logs to the shared folder, there was one thing with the token limits showin' up in the app.
[00:46] Sara: also security wanted to flag KMS integration questions, and a comment on audit log retention.
[00:55] Ava: Great. Quick status check — onboarding checklist from last week: we got IAM role created for Redwood Dedicated?
[01:06] Jon: yes, we created the role, but still need to confirm peering route and security groups, Liam sent a snippet but it didn't match our infra names.
[01:18] Liam: Right, I used a generic CIDR in the doc, my bad — I'll update with the correct ranges.
[01:25] Priya: On the ML side, we ran some warmup prompts, initial latency looked fine but costs spiked on long sequences, might be because caching wasnt enabled.
[01:37] Liam: That matches our expectation — KV cache wasn't turned on in the Dedicated test harness by default. We can enable prefix caching and set batching windows.
[01:48] Priya: Cool. We also saw some tokenization mismatch, like punctuation being tokenized differently between our tokenizer and the model, causing slight score drift.
[01:59] Ava: That's typical when tokenizers differ — we recommend using the model's tokenizer or mapping rules. We'll put recommended config in the test plan.
[02:12] Jon: Question on SSO — we need SAML with Okta, and ability to map groups to RBAC roles. Is that supported in the Private control plane?
[02:24] Liam: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support SAML/SSO mapping. For the hosted console there's also SSO. We'll share the SAML metadata and a step-by-step.
[02:37] Sara: And on encryption, how does KMS work? Do you support customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed?
[02:45] Ava: For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS (HSM on request) and fields are encrypted at rest. We'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[02:56] Priya: Great, please include a note about audit logs retention, we need 12 months for compliance.
[03:06] Liam: We can configure longer retention in the console; for Private we can ship logs to your SIEM.
[03:15] Priya: Thanks. Ok on the benchmark results — we ran three suites: short chat flows (avg 30 tokens), long generative docs (avg 800 tokens), and embeddings for search.
[03:28] Jon: Short flows averaged ~120ms p50 and 350ms p95 on your default hosted model per our runs. Long generative docs hit higher latencies and memory thrash on the 32GB instances.
[03:40] Liam: That 120ms looks low — I suspect there was conflation with client-side latency in the measurement. Did you split out server compute time?
[03:52] Priya: We tried but our instrumentation was at the app level only. We can re-run with the agent to capture server timings.
[04:03] Ava: We'll provide a lightweight script to isolate server vs network. Also we can suggest a Dedicated instance type tuned for long sequences — quantization helps but might affect quality.
[04:16] Priya: On quality, the long docs had minor hallucination drift after 600 tokens. Could be prompting or caching artifacts.
[04:27] Liam: Two levers: model variant and checkpointing/kv cache strategy. We can try a 16-bit variant with optimized kernels, or fallback to a higher-capacity model for long sequences.
[04:40] Jon: For cost, what tradeoffs do you have? We need predictable unit economics for forecasting.
[04:49] Ava: For Dedicated we provide reserved capacity pricing plus burst; unit cost is lower for reserved, and Redwood Optimize recommendations can reduce tokens via caching/aggregation. We'll send a sample forecast.
[05:01] Sara: Any compliance certificates — SOC2, ISO? We need evidence for procurement.
[05:07] Ava: Yes SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 for Redwood hosted. For Private we have a compliance pack and we support customer audits. I'll attach the certs.
[05:19] Priya: On data residency — we need EU region for patient PII. Can Dedicated be provisioned in eu-west-1?
[05:27] Liam: Yes, we have capacity there. For Private on-prem we'd do an air-gapped install if needed.
[05:36] Jon: Quick note — when we tried the model with our tokenizer the token counts were off which impacted cost estimation. Any tool to pre-tokenize?
[05:46] Liam: We'll share a small pre-tokenizer script and a notebook to estimate tokens. That's part of the 'sampling harness' in the test plan.
[05:56] Priya: Great, please put the harness in the shared drive. Also we want an automated daily smoke that hits the canary route.
[06:05] Ava: We can set up a canary job. For the pilot we recommend a canary + alerting for latency and error rate.
[06:15] Jon: About access, we tried to add the service account key but got a 403 from your onboarding API. Not sure if the role is missing permission.
[06:25] Liam: That usually means the role doesn't have the compute.serviceAgents or the peering wasn't in place. I'll follow up with a minimal IAM policy.
[06:36] Priya: When will we get Dedicated sizing? We're aiming for 2K qps short flows during business hours.
[06:45] Liam: We'll run capacity math after you send real traffic profiles. Tentatively, 4x A10 pools with autoscale to handle 2k qps depending on average tokens. We'll include baseline and headroom.
[06:56] Ava: Action item recap in a sec. Before that any open blockers?
[07:03] Sara: Security wants clarification on who can access logs in the console — need RBAC roles defined.
[07:10] Liam: We'll include an RBAC mapping doc— default roles are admin, engineer, observer and you can map SAML groups.
[07:20] Priya: Also curious about model fallbacks — if Dedicated is out of capacity can traffic failover to hosted?
[07:29] Ava: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible hosted variant per your policy. It's configurable per route and we can set throttles.
[07:39] Jon: For the pilot timeline — we want results by mid-June to present to the execs. Is that realistic?
[07:46] Ava: Yes, if we get dataset and access this week we can run the benchmarks and have consolidated results by 2027-06-14.
[07:56] Priya: We'll prioritise sending the data.
[08:01] Liam: I'll schedule the infra deep-dive with Jon to finalize VPC peering and IAM tomorrow.
[08:10] Ava: Ok wrapping up — I'll send the pricing/ SOC2/ KMS docs and the tokenization script after the call.
[08:18] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:22] Ava: Quick recap of next steps and action items — LMK if I missed anything.

Meeting recap (auto):
- Onboarding: IAM role present; VPC peering details need update; Liam to provide corrected CIDR & IAM policy.
- Access: SAML/Okta supported; Redwood to share SAML metadata; service account role permissions to be corrected.
- Security: KMS customer-managed supported for Dedicated; provide audit/SOC2 docs; log retention configurable.
- Benchmarks: Initial runs show short-flow p50 ~120ms (app-level), long flows have higher latency & memory issues; need server-side timings and harness rerun.
- Next steps: Redwood to share pricing, KMS and SOC2 docs; customer to send redacted dataset; SE to provide Dedicated sizing and test plan; schedule infra deep-dive.

End of transcript.
